q: In Next.js 16 with Cache Components, what gets cached by default?
options: Nothing, unless you add use cache
why: Caching is opt in. Before Next.js 16, the App Router cached some things by default, which surprised many people.

q: What is the cache key of a function marked 'use cache'?
options: Its arguments, and the values it uses from outside
why: getUser(1) and getUser(2) are two separate entries because the arguments are part of the key.

q: Which of these are true about updateTag?
options: The next visitor waits for fresh data
It can be called from a Route Handler
It only works in a Server Action
It is meant for read your own writes
why: updateTag expires the tag at once, so the next read waits for fresh data. It is only allowed in Server Actions. In a Route Handler, Next.js stops the build and tells you to use revalidateTag.

q: You call revalidateTag('posts', 'max'). What does the very next visitor get?
options: The old data, and the visitor after gets new data
The new data, and they wait for it
An error, until the cache is rebuilt
Nothing is changed until the deploy
why: This is stale while revalidate. The old copy is served at once and Next.js refreshes it in the background. I saw this on Next.js 16.4.6.

q: You can read cookies() inside a function marked 'use cache', because the cookie is part of the cache key.
why: No. Next.js stops the build. Read the cookie outside and pass the value in as an argument, so it becomes part of the key.

q: Which function sets how long a cached result stays fresh? (just the name)
why: cacheLife takes a profile name like 'hours' or a custom object with stale, revalidate and expire.
